preamble: The Proto-Indo-European voiced aspirated dental stop *dʰ became the voiceless labiodental fricative f in the Italic branch. The change ran through a voiceless dental fricative stage (*dʰ > *tʰ > *θ, Proto-Italic *θ) which then merged with *f. In Latin and Faliscan the outcome f is found only word-initially (word-medially Latin has d or b, as in medius 'middle' and ruber 'red'), whereas in the Sabellic languages (Oscan, Umbrian) *dʰ gives f in all positions. The change is confined to Italic and is one of the hallmark innovations of that branch.

examples.note: Word-initial *dʰ > f; related to fēmina 'woman' and fellō 'to suck'.
Extended form of the root *dʰeh₁- 'to put, place'.
Cognate with Ancient Greek θυμός and Sanskrit dhūmá-, which keep a dental.
Same initial f- reflex as Latin; Faliscan also has fīleo 'son' (cf. Latin fīlius).
Word-medial *dʰ also gives f in Sabellic, where Latin has d (medius).
Initial f- as in Latin faciō.
Medial *dʰ > f; Latin has ruber with b, and Oscan rufriis shows the same f.
